title: An analytically unramified local domain is N-1
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. If its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion is reduced, so $A$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified], then the integral closure of $A$ in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], i.e. $A$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

proof.text: Set-up. Write $\widehat A=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ for the $\mathfrak m$-adic completion of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and $\iota:A\to\widehat A$ for the canonical map. $\widehat A$ is a Noetherian ring by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]; it is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]; and it is $\mathfrak m\widehat A$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (1) ($\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated as $A$ is Noetherian). So $(\widehat A,\mathfrak m\widehat A)$ is a Noetherian complete local ring, hence a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata]. Moreover $\iota$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat] and faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. By hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified] $\widehat A$ is reduced. (These are the remarks after Definition 032X, lines 45791-45803, used at line 45824.) Lean uses AdicCompletion.isNoetherianRing and the Mathlib local-ring, completeness and flatness instances; Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom supplies faithful flatness.

source.place: Algebra, remarks after Definition Tag 032X, lines 45791-45803 (Lemmas 00MC, 05GH, 031C, 032W), used in the proof of Lemma Tag 032Y, line 45824

proof.text: A finite $\widehat A$-module $P$ inside the total ring of fractions of $\widehat A$. Let $\mathfrak p_1,\dots,\mathfrak p_s$ be the minimal primes of the reduced Noetherian ring $\widehat A$ and $Q(\widehat A)$ its total ring of fractions (the localization at the set of nonzerodivisors). By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] each $K_i=\widehat A_{\mathfrak p_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a field with $\mathfrak p_iK_i=0$, and the canonical map $Q(\widehat A)\to K_1\times\dots\times K_s$ is a ring isomorphism. Fix $i$ and put $D_i=\widehat A/\mathfrak p_i$, a domain. The kernel of $\widehat A\to K_i$, $a\mapsto a/1$, is $\mathfrak p_i$: it contains $\mathfrak p_i$ since $\mathfrak p_iK_i=0$, and if $a/1=0$ then $ua=0$ for some $u\notin\mathfrak p_i$, so $a\in\mathfrak p_i$ as $\mathfrak p_i$ is prime. So $D_i\subseteq K_i$, and every element $a/u$ of $K_i$ is $(a/1)(u/1)^{-1}$ with $u/1\ne0$; thus $K_i$ is the field of fractions of $D_i$. As $\widehat A$ is a Nagata ring (Step 1), $D_i$ is N-2 by [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], hence N-1 by [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] (take $L=K_i$): the integral closure $S_i$ of $D_i$ in $K_i$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $D_i$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], hence a finitely generated $\widehat A$-module through the surjection $\widehat A\to D_i$ (the same generators). Hence $P=S_1\times\dots\times S_s\subseteq K_1\times\dots\times K_s\cong Q(\widehat A)$ is a finitely generated $\widehat A$-module: the generators of the $S_i$, each placed in its own coordinate, generate it. (Stacks proves the equality $P=$ the integral closure of $\widehat A$ in $Q(\widehat A)$; only the inclusion of Step 4 is needed.) The private Lean helper finite_reduced_nagata_normalization maps integralClosure B (FractionRing B) into the finite product of integral closures in the residue fields. IsLocalization.algEquiv transports isN1_of_isN2 from each quotient fraction ring to its residue field; Module.Finite.trans restricts scalars. Compatibility and the residue-field bijections give injectivity.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 032Y (4), lines 45856-45871 (Lemmas 02LX and 032W)

proof.text: Embedding of $A'\otimes_A\widehat A$. Let $K$ be the fraction field of the domain $A$, $T=A\setminus\{0\}$, so $K=T^{-1}A$, and let $A'\subseteq K$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. (a) For $t\in T$, multiplication by $t$ is an injective $A$-linear map $A\to A$ ($A$ is a domain); since $\widehat A$ is flat over $A$ (Step 1, [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]), the induced map on $A\otimes_A\widehat A=\widehat A$, which is multiplication by $\iota(t)$, is injective: $\iota(T)$ consists of nonzerodivisors of $\widehat A$. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with $R=A$, multiplicative subset $T$, $R'=K$, $D=\widehat A$), $\widehat A\to K\otimes_A\widehat A$ is the localization of $\widehat A$ at $\iota(T)$. (c) Since $\iota(T)$ consists of nonzerodivisors, which are units in $Q(\widehat A)$, the universal property of this localization gives an $\widehat A$-algebra map $K\otimes_A\widehat A=\iota(T)^{-1}\widehat A\to Q(\widehat A)$, $a/\iota(t)\mapsto a/\iota(t)$; it is injective, because $a/\iota(t)=0$ in $Q(\widehat A)$ means $va=0$ for a nonzerodivisor $v$, so $a=0$. (d) The inclusion $A'\to K$ is an injective $A$-linear map, so by flatness $A'\otimes_A\widehat A\to K\otimes_A\widehat A$ is injective; it is a homomorphism of $\widehat A$-algebras. Composing (d) and (c) gives an injective $\widehat A$-algebra homomorphism $j:A'\otimes_A\widehat A\to Q(\widehat A)$. The private helper finite_tensor_normalization uses Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_of_nonZeroDivisors, IsLocalization.tensor, IsLocalization.liftAlgHom and Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap to construct the injection, with tensor factors in the order B tensor_R integralClosure R K.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 032Y (4), lines 45872-45874 ('As R -> R^ is flat we see that R' (x)_R R^ c Q(R) (x)_R R^ c Q(R^)'), written out for a domain R, where Q(R)=K

proof.text: The image of $j$ lies in $P$. $A'$ is integral over $A$ by its definition [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], so $A'\otimes_A\widehat A$ is integral over $\widehat A$ (via $a\mapsto1\otimes a$) by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change]. Let $z\in A'\otimes_A\widehat A$, with $z^n+c_{n-1}z^{n-1}+\dots+c_0=0$, $c_k\in\widehat A$. Applying the $\widehat A$-algebra map $j$ and then the projection $Q(\widehat A)\cong\prod_iK_i\to K_i$ (Step 2), the $i$-th component $x_i$ of $j(z)$ satisfies $x_i^n+\bar c_{n-1}x_i^{n-1}+\dots+\bar c_0=0$, where $\bar c_k\in D_i$ is the image of $c_k$ (the $\widehat A$-algebra structure of $K_i$ factors through $D_i\subseteq K_i$). So $x_i$ is integral over $D_i$, i.e. $x_i\in S_i$, for every $i$, and $j(z)\in P$. Hence $j(A'\otimes_A\widehat A)\subseteq P$. In Lean, Algebra.IsIntegral.tensorProduct and IsIntegral.map put the injection into integralClosure B (FractionRing B); no equality of normalizations is required.

proof.text: $A'\otimes_A\widehat A$ is a finite $\widehat A$-module generated by finitely many $f\otimes1$. Since $j$ is injective and $\widehat A$-linear (Step 3), $A'\otimes_A\widehat A\cong j(A'\otimes_A\widehat A)$, an $\widehat A$-submodule of the finitely generated $\widehat A$-module $P$ (Steps 2 and 4). As $\widehat A$ is Noetherian (Step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] shows that $A'\otimes_A\widehat A$ is a finitely generated $\widehat A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Each of finitely many generators is a finite sum $\sum_kf_k\otimes a_k=\sum_ka_k(f_k\otimes1)$ with $f_k\in A'$, $a_k\in\widehat A$; collecting the $f_k$ that occur gives $f_1,\dots,f_n\in A'$ such that the elements $f_1\otimes1,\dots,f_n\otimes1$ generate $A'\otimes_A\widehat A$ as an $\widehat A$-module. Module.Finite.of_injective supplies finiteness for both injections over the Noetherian ring B. The following descent theorem includes the pure-tensor generator argument internally.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 032Y (4), lines 45878-45881

proof.text: Descent by faithful flatness. Let $M\subseteq A'$ be the $A$-submodule generated by $f_1,\dots,f_n$, and consider the complex of $A$-modules $M\xrightarrow{u}A'\to0$ ($u$ the inclusion). Tensoring with $\widehat A$ gives $M\otimes_A\widehat A\xrightarrow{u\otimes1}A'\otimes_A\widehat A\to0$; the image of $u\otimes1$ is an $\widehat A$-submodule containing every $f_k\otimes1=(u\otimes1)(f_k\otimes1)$, so by Step 5 it is all of $A'\otimes_A\widehat A$, and the tensored complex is exact. As $A\to\widehat A$ is faithfully flat (Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]), the definition [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] (a complex is exact if and only if it is after tensoring with $\widehat A$) shows that $M\to A'\to0$ is exact, i.e. $A'=M$. Thus the integral closure $A'$ of $A$ in its fraction field is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], generated by $f_1,\dots,f_n$, which is the statement that $A$ is N-1 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. (In Stacks this is clause (4), with $Q(A)=K$ as $A$ is a domain, and clause (5) is its special case.) Lean closes this step with Module.Finite.of_finite_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat B.
